ratings_why.fun: One dial feeds two opposite builds, and the cast order with Lamp-Fanner, Burnished Brass and Lamplit Compounder is a real puzzle each turn; the early game is thin.
ratings_why.distinct: A count-to-7 Lamp that pays for stopping or for blowing over, and that can Flare mid-fight, plays unlike any of today's tribes; the Quacks pot and spell scaling are familiar parts.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken and v2 fixed the unclear cards; more passes would mostly change it, not improve it.

points.text: Say that 'after you cast a spell' effects resolve in reading order. Then putting Lamp-Fanner before or after Lamplit Compounder becomes a choice: Compounder reads 1 more Heat, or reads 0 if the Fanner's Stoke Flares.
The Old Lady makes 'exactly 7' easy: go over once and you land on 7. If she kept Heat where it was before the spell instead, The Spectacle players would still have to count.
Skep Pilferer is the one card that ignores the Lamp. Something like 'gain 1 gold when your Lamp Flares or The Old Lady catches it' would tie it to the dial.

The Alchymist pulls against Mother Shipton and the Compounder (Heat caps at 3), but it makes Burnt-Ring Senior and Eyed Hawk-moth Flare mid-fight every few hits. That is the best cross-build tension in the tribe; keep it.

standouts.why: Burnished Brass doubles every cast trigger at once: Heat, Fanner, Noctuid, Compounder, and the Uncertain Phial's dice roll.
The Alchymist moves the number other cards read, which flips The Spectacle from hard to easy and turns the fight into a Flare engine.
The Old Lady is a safety valve for one build and a card to sell for the other, so whether to sell her is a decision.

weakest.why: Skep Pilferer is generic once-a-turn gold with no link to Heat.
The Herald is a flat battery; the Tier-up Stoke helps only a little.
Treacle Painter's random target gives no placement or ordering choice.

flags.note: Dame Pavonia with Old Carbonaria in a Flare-heavy turn is well above the Tier 6 top end; the designer flags it too.
With The Alchymist, Eyed Hawk-moth and Mother Shipton, Burnt-Ring Senior can Flare several times a fight, and each Flare is a permanent board buff.
The Compounder with Brass and Fanner pays out per cast at high Heat; check its payout in a 6-cast turn.
